sources.title: RIT CSCI-518 Collaborative Seminar in Computer Graphics catalog description
sources.author: Rochester Institute of Technology
sources.content: This course examines current topics in Computer Graphics. This is intended to allow faculty to pilot potential new undergraduate offerings. Specific course details (such as prerequisites, course seminar, format, learning outcomes, assessment methods, and resource needs) will be determined by the faculty member(s) who propose a specific seminar course in this area. Specific course instances will be identified as belonging to the Computer Graphics and Visualization cluster. Enrollment in this course requires permission from the department offering the course. Contact Hours: Laboratory 3, Lecture 2

sources.title: OpenGL Specification and Reference
sources.author: Khronos Group
sources.content: The OpenGL graphics pipeline processes vertices through programmable shader stages. Primitive assembly groups vertices into points, lines, or triangles. Clipping removes portions outside the view volume. Rasterization converts primitives into fragment candidates. Interpolation produces per-fragment values from vertex outputs. Fragment processing computes values for framebuffer operations. Depth testing resolves visibility according to stored depth values. Blending combines a fragment result with an existing framebuffer value. Coordinate spaces, sampling, and numerical precision must remain explicit.

sources.title: MIT OpenCourseWare Introduction to Computer Graphics
sources.author: MIT OpenCourseWare
sources.content: Computer graphics uses geometric models to represent objects and scenes. Transformations position and orient geometry within coordinate systems. Viewing maps a scene through a camera model to an image. Rasterization samples projected primitives on a discrete pixel grid. Shading models how light, material, and geometry determine appearance. Texture mapping associates image data with geometric surfaces. Curves and surfaces provide compact smooth shape representations. Animation changes scene state over time. Ray tracing follows visibility and light paths through a scene. Visual correctness follows from explicit conventions, assumptions, sampling decisions, and measurable error.
